drivers.title: OPEC+ output nears pre-war levels and IEA sees Q4 surplus; oil heads for second weekly loss
drivers.rationale: Gulf producers have restored output around Hormuz and the IEA projects a surplus -> the remaining war premium in Brent near $96 erodes -> producers lag and airlines gain. Brent is already -12.8% in 20 days and mine incidents persist, so the size is moderate.

drivers.title: Oil falls for a third straight week on strong Middle East exports and higher US stocks; IEA sees lasting cut in Hormuz reliance
drivers.rationale: Exports via bypass routes are holding up, US stocks are building and a surplus is forecast -> the remaining war premium erodes -> producers lag. Brent is already -21% in 20 days, so most of the move is priced and the size is small.

drivers.title: Iran war grinds on with tanker mines, Gulf strikes and a third US carrier, but ceasefire odds rise as Trump calls new strikes unlikely
drivers.rationale: Headlines stress attacks, but the money points the other way: US-Iran ceasefire odds rose 10-12 points (56% by 30 Nov, 84% by year-end) and Brent fell again -> the escalation premium keeps fading -> energy majors lag airlines. Mine incidents persist and a risk-off market hurts airlines, so confidence is low.
